moves.name: word-portal
moves.title: Word portal
moves.use: a typed word grows until one stem is the whole frame and the next scene shows through the letterforms (an SVG text clip over a fixed scene B), on a log-path zoom
moves.useWhen: a typed word is on screen and the next scene should appear inside its letters: the word grows until one stem is the whole frame, and scene B shows through the letterforms the whole way. The word is the shared element, and it is a window, not a filled shape. The detail that sells it is that B is fixed and the letters move over it, so the view through the glyphs slides like a real window until the stem is wider than the frame and B is all there is.

The word is the shared element, and it is a window, not a filled shape. The detail that sells it is that B is fixed and the letters move over it, so the view through the glyphs slides like a real window until the stem is wider than the frame and B is all there is.
moves.codeHtml:
html
<svg width="0" height="0"><defs><clipPath id="portal" clipPathUnits="userSpaceOnUse"><text id="ptext"></text></clipPath></defs></svg>
<section class="b" style="clip-path: url(#portal)">...scene B, its ground in the colour of the word...</section>
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; the typed characters are the film's keys, and the growth needs no extra cue.
moves.notesHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
import { easeFn } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const swap = easeFn('swap'), land = easeFn('land');
const T0 = 1.6, DUR = 1.15, STEM = 0.19;                             // STEM: ink width of the first letter's stem as a share of the font size
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const ext = measure.getExtentOfChar(0);                            // a hidden copy of the full word, so the aim does not move while it types
  const ox = ext.x + ext.width / 2, oy = Y0 - 0.37 * F;              // the middle of the stem of the first letter
  const S = (1.15 * W) / (STEM * F);
  const q = clamp((t - T0) / DUR), p = 0.4 * q + 0.6 * swap(q), s = Math.exp(Math.log(S) * p);   // log path: equal steps read as equal speed
  const px = ox + (W / 2 - ox) * p, py = oy + (H / 2 - oy) * p;      // the stem drifts to the middle as it grows
  ptext.textContent = WORD.slice(0, typed);
  ptext.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${px - s * ox} ${py - s * oy}) scale(${s})`);
  caret.style.transform = `translate(${px - s * ox}px, ${py - s * oy}px) scale(${s})`;   // the caret grows with the word
  b.style.clipPath = q >= 1 ? 'none' : 'url(#portal)';               // the stem covers the frame: drop the mask
  pops.forEach((el, i) => { el.style.translate = `0 ${(1 - land(clamp((t - T0 - 0.1 - i * 0.12) / 0.7))) * 7 * u}px`; });
});
  • Z-order: scene A (ground, label, caret) under, scene B over it, clipped by the glyphs. A is never faded: it is whatever the letters do not cover.
  • Scene B's ground is the colour of the typed word, so the typed word is B's ground seen through the letters. At the first frame of the growth nothing changes on screen. B's own elements then arrive inside the glyphs, and that is when the viewer sees a scene in the type.
  • Aim at the stem of a letter with a plain vertical stem (l, I, T). A round letter has no stem to fill the frame. The scale is 1.15 * W / (STEM * F), about 41 for a 26 u word, which is why the growth runs on a log path and ends with the stem opening as a tall window across the frame.
  • B's elements sit away from the typed word's first position, or they show inside the letters before the move starts. B is graphic, not a line of text: three format tiles sit in the middle of the frame, so the letters show whole tiles while they grow, and the headline and URL arrive after them. The word is centred on the frame, so the stem has a short way to the middle.
  • The word types at 0.14 s a letter and the portal opens on a lit caret after two blinks.
  • What goes wrong: a thin face leaves no window, so use weight 800 or more. Leaving the clip-path on after the stem is wider than the frame costs a huge path for nothing. A caret in a layer that does not take the same matrix stays behind and reads as a cut.

moves.title: Underline road
moves.use: the underline of a headline extends, bends down and becomes the route on a simple map, with the camera trailing the head at its speed and stopping at the map's end
moves.useWhen: a line must become a route: one blue stroke draws along real streets from a start dot to a destination pin, and the result card shows the time. The stroke is one path with one dash offset, so its head never jumps at a corner.
moves.sound: none; the pin landing is the one point a cue could use.
moves.useHtml: Use when a line must become a route: one blue stroke draws along real streets from a start dot to a destination pin, and the result card shows the time. The stroke is one path with one dash offset, so its head never jumps at a corner.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const pts = [[VX[1], HY[3]], [VX[1], HY[2]], [VX[3], HY[2]], [VX[3], HY[1]], [VX[4], HY[1]]];   // street centres: start, three turns, destination
const R = 38;                                                       // corners are quadratic curves, radius 38 units
const total = line.getTotalLength();
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const s = total * easeFn('settle')(clamp((t - 1.0) / 1.9));   // 1.9 s: a long travel that starts and ends at rest takes settle
  [casing, line].forEach((p) => { p.style.strokeDasharray = `${total} ${total}`; p.style.strokeDashoffset = total - s; });

moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; the pin landing is the one point a cue could use.
moves.notesHtml:
How it looks and moves

  • The clip copies a maps app in its light style: pale land, grey building footprints, white minor streets with a grey casing, yellow main streets, a green park, a blue river, and a street name on every street, in grey with a white halo.
  • The route is the app blue (#4285f4) with a darker casing, 11 units wide, rounded at the turns. It runs on street centres, never across a block.
  • Order: the directions card (start and destination) fades in at 0.25 s, the start dot shows at 0.7 s with a slow pulse, the route draws from 1.0 s to 2.9 s, the pin drops 30 units and fades in over 0.25 s (the start address on the card, 22 Mill Lane, is the street the route starts on), then the time card fades in at 3.2 s.
  • The map does not pan or cut: the route preview fits the whole route on one screen, as the real app does. No spring or overshoot: the line takes settle and the pin takes land.
  • The map is our own invented city (Cedar, Pine, Mill, Elm). Names and numbers are made up.
  • Common mistake: the card names a start street that is not where the dot sits, or a card covers a street label. Start the card and the route on the same street, and keep the time card over blocks, not labels.
  • The card text is 3.4 to 4.4 percent of the frame height, so it reads at once.

moves.name: caret-door
moves.title: Caret door
moves.use: the blinking caret grows tall, then opens as a two-frame-wide door that turns about it under perspective; the next screen is on the door's face
moves.useWhen: a typed command is done and the next screen should open out of the caret. The clip copies a shell: the command runs, the output prints, and the block caret waits on the next prompt. Then the caret grows tall and becomes the hinge of a door. The door turns open under perspective and shows the next screen (a video player with its controls and the three formats). There is no cut and no crossfade.
moves.sound: none; a key tick per typed character is the film's, and the door adds no cue of its own.
moves.useHtml: Use when a typed command is done and the next screen should open out of the caret. The clip copies a shell: the command runs, the output prints, and the block caret waits on the next prompt. Then the caret grows tall and becomes the hinge of a door. The door turns open under perspective and shows the next screen (a video player with its controls and the three formats). There is no cut and no crossfade.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { easeFn } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const land = easeFn('land'), settle = easeFn('settle'), launch = easeFn('launch');
const T_GROW = 3.0, D_GROW = 0.5, T_OPEN = 3.5, D_OPEN = 0.9, RETRACT = 0.3, PERSPECTIVE = 1.7 * W;
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const r = nextPrompt.getBoundingClientRect(), cx = r.right + 1.2 * u, cy = (r.top + r.bottom) / 2;   // the caret sits at the end of the prompt
  const g = land(clamp((t - T_GROW) / D_GROW)), dip = Math.sin(Math.PI * clamp((t - T_GROW + 0.12) / 0.12)) * 0.08;   // gather 8 percent, then rise
  const h = (4.8 * u * (1 - dip) + (1.04 * H - 4.8 * u) * g) * (1 - launch(clamp((t - T_OPEN) / RETRACT)));
  const cw = 2.4 * u - 1.2 * u * g;                                  // the block narrows to a bar as it grows
  Object.assign(caret.style, { left: `${cx - cw / 2}px`, width: `${cw}px`, height: `${h}px`, top: `${cy - h / 2 + (H / 2 - cy) * g}px` });
  door.style.left = `${cx - W}px`; door.style.width = `${2 * W}px`;   // two frames wide, centred on the caret
  face.style.left = `${W - cx}px`;                                     // the screen on the door lines up with the frame when it lands
  door.style.visibility = t >= T_OPEN ? 'visible' : 'hidden';
  door.style.transform = `perspective(${PERSPECTIVE}px) rotateY(${90 * (1 - settle(clamp((t - T_OPEN) / D_OPEN)))}deg)`;
  win.style.display = t > T_OPEN + D_OPEN + 0.05 ? 'none' : 'flex';   // the door covers the shell: remove it, so the exit shows empty ground
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; a key tick per typed character is the film's, and the door adds no cue of its own.
moves.notesHtml:
• The shell types and prints in whole steps, as a terminal does. The caret is a solid block while keys arrive and blinks every 0.28 s on the last prompt.
  • Order, bottom to top: the shell, the door, the caret. The door starts edge-on under the caret, so its first visible frame is a sliver beside a bar of the same height. The caret then draws back to nothing on EASE.launch in 0.3 s, as the axis the door turns on.
  • The door turns on EASE.settle in 0.9 s. A fast-start ease makes the leaf jump to half open in two frames, because the width of a leaf that turns from edge-on goes with the sine of the angle.
  • Perspective is 1.7 frame widths. Less makes the far side collapse to a point. More flattens the swing.
  • The door is 1.4 frames tall, so its far edge still covers the top and bottom while the angle is small.
  • The player progress and its time run from the landing, so the page is alive in the hold.

Common mistake: a door narrower than two frames leaves a strip of the shell at one side when it lands. Hinging at the left edge of the door puts the caret on the edge, not in the middle of the opening.

moves.name: word-sweep
moves.title: Word colour sweep
moves.use: the accent runs word by word in reading order and stays on the target word
moves.useWhen: a headline is already on screen and one word is the point. The accent runs word by word in reading order, lifting each from dim to white as it passes, and stays on the target word. Every device directs the eye; this one names its target in the markup.
moves.sound: none; the colour points the eye without a sound.
moves.snippet: every device directs the eye
moves.useHtml: Use when a headline is already on screen and one word is the point. The accent runs word by word in reading order, lifting each from dim to white as it passes, and stays on the target word. Every device directs the eye; this one names its target in the markup.
moves.codeHtml:
html
<h1>every device directs the eye</h1>
<style>h1 { color: var(--dim); } h1 span { display: inline-block; white-space: pre; }</style>
<script type="module">
import { EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const h1 = document.querySelector('h1');
const words = h1.textContent.split(' ').map((w, i, a) =>
  Object.assign(document.createElement('span'), { textContent: i < a.length - 1 ? w + ' ' : w }));
h1.replaceChildren(...words);
const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
const dim = css.getPropertyValue('--dim'), ink = css.getPropertyValue('--ink'), accent = css.getPropertyValue('--accent');
const beat = 150, step = 140;   // ms; step is faster than reading (about 250 ms a word), so the sweep leads the eye
words.forEach((s, i) => {
  const last = i === words.length - 1;
  s.animate([{ color: dim }, { color: accent, offset: 0.25 }, { color: last ? accent : ink }],
    { duration: 520, delay: beat + i * step, easing: EASE.land, fill: 'both' });
});
</script>
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; the colour points the eye without a sound.
moves.notesHtml:
Three colours, in this order: --dim (#5c5b63 on #16151a, readable but quiet), --ink for what has been read, --accent for one word at a time. The target is the only word that stays accent. A step slower than 250 ms follows the reader instead of leading; a step under 100 ms is a flicker. For a target in the middle of the line, sweep to it and stop: the words after it stay dim.

h1 { font: 200 18vh/1 'Archivo', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.02em;

@keyframes thicken { to { font-weight: 900; letter-spacing: -0.04em; } }
moves.soundHtml: Sound: bloom at --beat-1; its low, slow body matches the word getting heavier (default gain).
moves.notesHtml:
html
<h1>weight</h1>
<script type="module">
import { EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--settle', EASE.land);
</script>

Start at 200, not 100: a hairline at 100 vanishes against a dark ground and the first frames read as empty. Tighten letter-spacing with the weight (heavy type wants less air) so the word grows denser, not only wider. The @font-face must declare the range 100 900; with a single weight the browser synthesises bold and nothing morphs.

moves.name: marker-highlight
moves.title: Marker highlight
moves.use: a highlighter bar wipes behind one phrase and the text flips dark for contrast
moves.useWhen: one phrase in a line of text must be picked out the way a person does it on a page: with a highlighter pen.
moves.sound: none, or a soft pen drag under each pass (a noise swish at 0.5 s).
moves.useHtml:
Use when one phrase in a line of text must be picked out the way a person does it on a page: with a highlighter pen.

Look: dark text on the flat neutral ground. The mark is translucent yellow with mix-blend-mode: multiply, so the text stays dark and the ground shows through. It covers the lower two thirds of the line, tilts about half a degree and has ragged, uneven ends. A second pen pass over the same words overlaps the first and goes darker where they meet, as ink does.

How it moves: the pen is a slanted edge that crosses the word in 0.55 to 0.65 s on EASE.settle. A pass can go left to right or back. The text does not move. After the last pass the page holds, then leaves on leave.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { EASE } from '/core/motion/presets.js';
const stroke = (wipe, atMs, ms, rtl = false) => {
  const hide = rtl ? 'polygon(112% 0, 112% 0, 120% 100%, 112% 100%)' : 'polygon(-12% 0, -12% 0, -20% 100%, -12% 100%)';
  const show = rtl ? 'polygon(-8% 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%)' : 'polygon(0 0, 108% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%)';
  wipe.animate([{ clipPath: hide }, { clipPath: show }], { duration: ms, delay: atMs, easing: EASE.settle, fill: 'both' });
};
stroke(wipes[0], 500, 650);          // .wipe: absolute inset 0, mix-blend-mode: multiply, holds the .bar
stroke(wipes[1], 1700, 650);         // .bar: #ffe14d, rotate(-0.5deg), clip-path with an uneven outline
stroke(wipes[2], 2300, 550, true);   // a second pass, right to left, on a taller .bar
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none, or a soft pen drag under each pass (a noise swish at 0.5 s).
moves.notesHtml:
Common mistake: an opaque solid box with light text. A real highlighter is see-through and the text stays dark. Use multiply, a pale yellow, and an uneven outline, never a brand fill.

moves.name: underline-draw
moves.title: Underline draw
moves.use: a line draws under the key word, left to right, fast in and slow out
moves.useWhen: one key word needs emphasis after it lands: a line draws under it from left to right, fast at the start and slow at the end, like a pen.
moves.sound: none; the line points at a word the viewer is already reading.
moves.useHtml: Use when one key word needs emphasis after it lands: a line draws under it from left to right, fast at the start and slow at the end, like a pen.
moves.codeHtml:
css
.key { position: relative; display: inline-block; }
.key svg { position: absolute; left: -0.02em; top: 100%; width: 104%; height: 0.24em; overflow: visible; }
.key path { fill: none; stroke: var(--accent); stroke-width: 7; stroke-linecap: round;
            stroke-dasharray: 1; stroke-dashoffset: 1;
            animation-name: draw; animation-duration: 0.6s; animation-delay: var(--beat-1);
            animation-timing-function: var(--draw); animation-fill-mode: both; }

moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; the line points at a word the viewer is already reading.
moves.notesHtml:
html
<span class="key">noticed<svg viewBox="0 0 300 20" preserveAspectRatio="none"><path pathLength="1" d="M4 12 C 70 5, 190 4, 296 9"/></svg></span>

--draw is EASE.land. pathLength="1" lets the dash be 1 whatever the real length is, so the same two lines work for any path.

The numbers that make it look expensive

  • 0.6 s on EASE.land: two thirds of the line is out in the first 0.15 s, the last third takes the rest.
  • The path is a slight curve (ends 5 units apart in a 20 unit box), not a ruler line. A straight line reads as a border.
  • Round caps, and a stroke about 0.06em thick at this size. Thin lines vanish in a 640 px clip.
  • The line starts 0.1 to 0.2 s after the word is readable, so the word lands first.

The common mistake

Placing the line at the baseline. It strikes through descenders (g, y, p). top: 100% on a line-height: 1.2 box puts it below them. Also: preserveAspectRatio="none" stretches the stroke with the box. For a very long word, draw the SVG at real pixel size instead.

moves.name: bracket-callout
moves.title: Bracket callout
moves.use: corner brackets fly in and snap onto a word or a UI part with a small overshoot
moves.useWhen: the eye must go to one word or one part of a UI: four corner brackets fly in from outside, snap onto the target box and land with a small overshoot.
moves.sound: pluck at --beat-1 + 0.20 s, when the corners first reach the box and snap (default gain).
moves.useHtml: Use when the eye must go to one word or one part of a UI: four corner brackets fly in from outside, snap onto the target box and land with a small overshoot.
moves.codeHtml:

.c { position: absolute; width: var(--arm); height: var(--arm); border: 0 solid var(--accent); opacity: 0;
     animation-duration: 0.55s; animation-delay: var(--beat-1);
     animation-timing-function: var(--land); animation-fill-mode: both; }
.tl { left: 0; top: 0; border-width: var(--w) 0 0 var(--w); border-top-left-radius: var(--rad); animation-name: tl; }
/* tr, bl, br: the same with the other two borders and the other two corners */
@keyframes tl { from { translate: calc(var(--far) * -1) calc(var(--far) * -1); opacity: 0; }
                12% { opacity: 1; } to { translate: 0 0; opacity: 1; } }
moves.soundHtml: Sound: pluck at --beat-1 + 0.20 s, when the corners first reach the box and snap (default gain).
moves.notesHtml:
html
<span class="target">Export<span class="frame"><i class="c tl"></i><i class="c tr"></i><i class="c bl"></i><i class="c br"></i></span></span>

--land is EASE.pop. The curve passes 1, so each corner travels 5 to 10 percent past the box (toward the target's centre) and comes back.

The numbers that make it look expensive

  • Each corner travels --far (13u) along the diagonal, in 0.55 s. All four run at once, so the frame looks like one object closing in.
  • The overshoot dips the brackets inside the frame for about 60 ms: this is the "snap".
  • The frame sits 1.6u outside the target's own box (u is 1 percent of frame height), so it never touches the text. Arms are 3.6u, about a third of the target height, with a 0.8u corner radius.
  • Opacity reaches 1 in the first 12 percent, so the brackets are never seen fading.
  • Only the accent draws. The target does not change colour; the brackets are the whole signal.

The common mistake

Scaling one bordered box down onto the target. The stroke shrinks with the scale, the corner radius distorts, and the four sides are visible the whole way. Move four separate corners instead: strokes stay one width and only the corners travel.

moves.name: spotlight-dim
moves.title: Spotlight dim
moves.use: the frame dims around one target: a hole closes from the full frame onto it and its shadow is the dim
moves.useWhen: a screen with several parts is on and one of them is the point. A rounded hole starts as the whole frame and closes onto the target; its own box-shadow is the dim, so everything outside the hole falls to 20 percent and the target is the only thing lit. The target leans in 4 percent on the same curve.
moves.sound: none; the dim points the eye without a sound.
moves.snippet:
.hole { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; border-radius: 0;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax rgba(10, 9, 13, 0.8); pointer-events: none; }
moves.useHtml:
Status: a UI scrim, not a light. The hole is a dim over a screen that points the eye (its box-shadow is a veil, not light). For a real lit-screen look (bloom, depth of field on a tilted screen) use the lens: lens, core/surfaces/lens.js.

Use when a screen with several parts is on and one of them is the point. A rounded hole starts as the whole frame and closes onto the target; its own box-shadow is the dim, so everything outside the hole falls to 20 percent and the target is the only thing lit. The target leans in 4 percent on the same curve.
moves.codeHtml:
css
.hole { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; border-radius: 0;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax rgba(10, 9, 13, 0.8); pointer-events: none; }
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; the dim points the eye without a sound.
moves.notesHtml:
js
import { EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const pad = '0.6vh';
hole.animate([
  { left: '0px', top: '0px', width: '100vw', height: '100vh', borderRadius: '0px' },
  { left: `calc(14vw - ${pad})`, top: `calc(52vh - ${pad})`, width: `calc(35vw + 2 * ${pad})`, height: `calc(34vh + 2 * ${pad})`, borderRadius: '3.6vh' }],
  { duration: 800, delay: 150, easing: EASE.landSoft, fill: 'both' });
target.animate([{ scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.04 }], { duration: 800, delay: 150, easing: EASE.landSoft, fill: 'both' });

The hole closes from the whole frame, so the dim arrives as the light narrows and never fades in as a flat veil. Match the hole radius to the target radius plus its padding (3 vh + 0.6 vh here) or a lit corner shows. Keep the dim at 0.75 to 0.85: lower and the rest still competes, higher and the context is lost. A padding over 1.5 vh reads as a frame border, which is banned. Use calc() with literal lengths in the keyframes; var() in a keyframe does not interpolate.

moves.name: hand-drawn-notes
moves.title: Hand drawn notes
moves.use: a person's margin notes: a loose circle round one word, an arrow from a written label and an underline, drawn on with stroke-dashoffset and a seeded wobble
moves.useWhen: a held line needs the margin notes of a person: a loose circle around one word, an arrow from a written label to it, and an underline under another, each drawn on like a pen. Every stroke is an SVG path revealed with stroke-dashoffset, built with a seeded wobble, so the marks are uneven and the same on every render.
moves.sound: none; or a dry pen scratch under each stroke, as a short recorded effect.
moves.useHtml: Use when a held line needs the margin notes of a person: a loose circle around one word, an arrow from a written label to it, and an underline under another, each drawn on like a pen. Every stroke is an SVG path revealed with stroke-dashoffset, built with a seeded wobble, so the marks are uneven and the same on every render.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const rand = rng(7);                                  // core/motion/springs.js: seeded, never Math.random
const wob = (amount) => (rand() * 2 - 1) * amount;
// a circle of 1.06 turns whose radius drifts out 7 percent, so the end overshoots the start
const ring = Array.from({ length: 14 }, (_, i) => {
  const a = -2.5 + (i / 12) * Math.PI * 2 * 1.06, grow = 1 + (i / 13) * 0.07 + wob(0.025);
  return [cx + Math.cos(a) * rx * grow, cy + Math.sin(a) * ry * grow];
});
function stroke(d, at, dur, easing) {                 // d: Catmull-Rom points written as cubic Beziers
  const p = document.createElementNS(NS, 'path');
  p.setAttribute('d', d); p.setAttribute('pathLength', '1');
  svg.append(p);
  p.animate([{ strokeDashoffset: 1 }, { strokeDashoffset: 0 }], { delay: at * 1000, duration: dur * 1000, easing, fill: 'both' });
}
stroke(smooth(ring), 0.45, 0.6, EASE.settle);
label.animate([{ clipPath: 'inset(-10% 100% -10% 0)' }, { clipPath: 'inset(-10% 0 -10% 0)' }], { delay: 1100, duration: 450, fill: 'both' });
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; or a dry pen scratch under each stroke, as a short recorded effect.
moves.notesHtml:
css
svg path { fill: none; stroke: var(--accent); stroke-linecap: round; stroke-dasharray: 1; stroke-dashoffset: 1; }
.label { font: 700 9vh/1 'Caveat', cursive; color: var(--accent); }

The numbers that make it look expensive

  • Order is the story: circle (0.6 s), then the label writes on (0.45 s) while the arrow draws from it to the circle (0.35 s) and its head flicks in (0.2 s), then the underline (0.45 s). Strokes overlap by a third.
  • A pen starts slow, runs, and stops: EASE.settle for the long strokes, EASE.landSoft only for the arrow head.
  • The wobble is small and seeded: 2.5 percent of the radius on the circle, 1 percent of the font size on the shaft. More reads as a bad drawing, none as a vector ellipse.
  • The circle overshoots its start by 6 percent of a turn: a closed circle is a shape, an overlapped one is a gesture.
  • The label is written on a hard left-to-right clip, not a fade, and sits in a handwriting face (Caveat) against the sans line. One accent colour for every mark, 4.5:1 on the ground.
  • Underline under the descender line of the word, as in underline-draw.md, with a slight sag.

The common mistake

Using Math.random for the wobble, or a fresh draw per frame: the strokes shiver and no two renders match. Seed once at load. Also draw the marks after the line has landed; strokes on a moving word slip off it.

moves.name: ui-focus-zoom
moves.title: UI focus zoom
moves.use: zoom onto one part of a captured UI: the cursor lands, then one translate and one scale put the part in the middle
moves.useWhen: a captured screen is on and one part of it is the point: a status, a button, a number. The cursor lands on the part first, then the whole screen scales until that part fills about a third of the frame width and its centre sits in the middle. The camera is one translate and one scale on the same ease, so the target travels straight to the centre.
moves.sound: none; the cursor landing is the cue's job in cursor-click, and the zoom itself is silent.
moves.useHtml: Use when a captured screen is on and one part of it is the point: a status, a button, a number. The cursor lands on the part first, then the whole screen scales until that part fills about a third of the frame width and its centre sits in the middle. The camera is one translate and one scale on the same ease, so the target travels straight to the centre.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const world = document.querySelector('.world');            // transform-origin: 0 0
const r = target.getBoundingClientRect();                   // measured before any animation runs
const W = innerWidth, H = innerHeight;
const s = (0.36 * W) / r.width;                             // the target fills 36% of the frame width
const tx = W * 0.5 - s * (r.left + r.width / 2), ty = H * 0.5 - s * (r.top + r.height / 2);
cursor.animate([{ translate: '-16vw 12vh' }, { translate: '0 0' }],
  { duration: 500, delay: 50, easing: EASE.landSoft, fill: 'both' });
world.animate([{ translate: '0 0', scale: 1 }, { translate: `${tx}px ${ty}px`, scale: s }],
  { duration: 1000, delay: 550, easing: EASE.landSoft, fill: 'both' });
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; the cursor landing is the cue's job in cursor-click, and the zoom itself is silent.
moves.notesHtml:
The individual translate and scale properties apply as translate then scale from the origin, so p -> t + s * p and the target lands exactly on the frame centre. Measure the rect once at load, never per frame. Start the camera 50 ms after the cursor lands, so the eye is on the target when the move begins. A scale of 2.5 to 4 reads as a zoom; past 5 the capture goes soft. EASE.landSoft gives a firm start and a long soft arrival; use EASE.settle for a calmer film. Cut back out on the next beat, never zoom back on a mirror curve. A snap zoom (a punch) runs 150 to 250 ms; a zoom to focus takes 400 to 800 ms. A zoom earns its place only when it directs attention, shows hierarchy or bridges a cut. If a pan-stations camera owns the .world, fold the zoom into that camera's one translate and scale: two transforms on one world stack, and the target lands off centre.

moves.name: caret-follow
moves.title: Caret follow
moves.use: the camera trails the typing caret on a soft spring, so a long line stays readable at close range
moves.useWhen: a command or a line is typed and the camera is close enough that the line runs past the frame. The camera does not pan on a timer: it is a spring behind the caret, so it trails by a fraction of a second, speeds up on a burst of letters and rests on a pause. The text behind the caret stays in view and the text ahead of it is never shown early. It is the terminal camera of the vawe-flow-2 film.
moves.sound: pluck at 0.23 s into the move (the first character) and at the last value in at (the last character) (default gain); never one per character.
moves.useHtml: Use when a command or a line is typed and the camera is close enough that the line runs past the frame. The camera does not pan on a timer: it is a spring behind the caret, so it trails by a fraction of a second, speeds up on a burst of letters and rests on a pause. The text behind the caret stays in view and the text ahead of it is never shown early. It is the terminal camera of the vawe-flow-2 film.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
import { track, rng } from '../../core/motion/springs.js';
const s = 1.9, ch = caret.getBoundingClientRect().width;     // monospace: a caret is one character wide
const x0 = line.left + promptWidth, y = line.top + line.height / 2, winLeft = win.getBoundingClientRect().left;
const rand = rng(7);                                          // seeded: the same rhythm on every render
let clock = 0.2;
const at = [...text].map((c) => { clock += 0.026 + rand() * 0.024 + (c === ' ' ? 0.07 : 0); return clock; });
const keys = [[0, x0], ...at.map((t, i) => [t, x0 + (i + 1) * ch])];   // the caret x after each character

vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const n = at.filter((a) => a <= t).length;                  // characters typed at t; show text.slice(0, n)
  const follow = track(t, keys, 90, 20);                      // one soft spring per character
  const tx = Math.min(W * 0.66 - s * follow, W * 0.05 - s * winLeft);   // caret rests at 66% of the width; never show past the window edge
  world.style.transform = `translate(${tx}px, ${H * 0.5 - s * y}px) scale(${s})`;   // world { transform-origin: 0 0 }
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: pluck at 0.23 s into the move (the first character) and at the last value in at (the last character) (default gain); never one per character.
moves.notesHtml:
The camera keeps a physical spring on purpose: it is a sum of one spring per character, and no single EASE segment trails a moving target. The stiffness is the feel: track(t, keys, 90, 20) trails by about 0.2 s (2 x damping ratio / natural frequency). At k 170 the camera locks to every letter and shakes; under 60 it drifts behind the text. The caret rests at two thirds of the width so the eye reads the last 15 or so characters. The min() stops the camera from showing the empty ground left of the window at the start. Every input is a function of t, so the frame does not depend on the last one. Blink only after the typing ends, so the tail is alive. A typo or a backspace is a lower n in the same table (a [t, text] state list, latest state with t passed), never a mutated string.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: pull-back-reveal
moves.title: Pull back reveal
moves.use: open tight on a detail and pull back to the whole; scale runs on a log path so the speed reads even
moves.useWhen: a film opens on a detail and the whole should arrive as an answer: a status dot, a letter, one number. The first frame is tight on the detail (9x), and the camera pulls back to the full composition. The detail is the hook and the wide frame is the payoff.
moves.sound: bloom at 0.10 s into the move, when the pull back leaves the detail, so the film has sound from its first beat (default gain).
moves.useHtml: Use when a film opens on a detail and the whole should arrive as an answer: a status dot, a letter, one number. The first frame is tight on the detail (9x), and the camera pulls back to the full composition. The detail is the hook and the wide frame is the payoff.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
import { easeFn } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const r = dot.getBoundingClientRect();                     // measured before the first frame
const d = { x: r.left + r.width / 2, y: r.top + r.height / 2 }, c = { x: innerWidth / 2, y: innerHeight / 2 };
const s0 = 9, t0 = 0.1, dur = 1.6;                         // world { transform-origin: 0 0 }
const ease = easeFn('land');     // fast, then a long soft arrival
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const u = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (t - t0) / dur)), p = ease(u);
  const s = Math.exp(Math.log(s0) * (1 - p));              // zoom is multiplicative: scale on a log path
  const cam = { x: d.x + (c.x - d.x) * p, y: d.y + (c.y - d.y) * p };   // the dot is centred first, the card last
  world.style.transform = `translate(${c.x - s * cam.x}px, ${c.y - s * cam.y}px) scale(${s})`;
  const sb = Math.pow(s, 0.55);                            // the ground scales less, so it reads as far behind
  ground.style.transform = `translate(${c.x - sb * cam.x}px, ${c.y - sb * cam.y}px) scale(${sb})`;
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: bloom at 0.10 s into the move, when the pull back leaves the detail, so the film has sound from its first beat (default gain).
moves.notesHtml:
Interpolating scale linearly from 9 to 1 spends its first frames at a speed the eye cannot follow and its last ones crawling; the log path keeps each frame the same percentage larger. The camera centre moves from the detail to the frame centre on the same p, so the detail leaves the middle as the card arrives. The ground layer needs a box much larger than the frame (here 700 vw) with transform-origin at the frame origin, or its edge shows at 9x. Hold the tight frame 0.1 s, not longer: the detail must be a hook, not a still. The tight frame needs one clear subject and nothing half-cropped beside it.

moves.name: parallax-dive
moves.title: Parallax dive
moves.use: the camera flies forward through layers at real depths: near layers rush past, the far ground barely moves; also one camera move on ground, mid and front layers by depth (parallax())
moves.useWhen: a title should arrive by flying into a scene, not by appearing in it. Layers sit at real depths in CSS 3D; the camera moves forward through them, so near layers rush past the frame edge, mid cards drift outward and the far dots barely move. The title starts small and deep and ends at scale 1. The speed differences are the depth; nothing is faked with per-layer offsets.
moves.sound: none; the dive is space, and a whoosh on it reads as a cheap trailer.
moves.useHtml: Use when a title should arrive by flying into a scene, not by appearing in it. Layers sit at real depths in CSS 3D; the camera moves forward through them, so near layers rush past the frame edge, mid cards drift outward and the far dots barely move. The title starts small and deep and ends at scale 1. The speed differences are the depth; nothing is faked with per-layer offsets.
moves.codeHtml:
css
.stage { position: absolute; inset: 0; perspective: 80vh; perspective-origin: 50% 50%; }
.rig   { position: absolute; inset: 0; transform-style: preserve-3d; }
.layer { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%;
         translate: calc(var(--x) * 1vw - 50%) calc(var(--y) * 1vh - 50%);
         transform: translateZ(calc(var(--z) * 1vh)); }   /* depth in vh: --z -240 far, -120 title, +30 near */
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; the dive is space, and a whoosh on it reads as a cheap trailer.
moves.notesHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
import { easeFn } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const t0 = 0.1, dur = 1.8, dive = 120;                     // dive: camera travel in vh, so the title (z -120) ends at z 0
const ease = easeFn('land');
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const p = ease(Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (t - t0) / dur))), vh = innerHeight / 100;
  rig.style.transform = `translate3d(${-3 * p * vh * 0.5625}px, 0, ${dive * p * vh}px)`;   // a small sideways drift adds parallax
  near.forEach((n) => { n.style.opacity = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (52 - dive * p) / 22)); });
});

A layer at depth z is drawn at P / (P - z - travel) of its size, P being the perspective (80 vh), so a layer with z + travel near 80 vh fills the frame: fade the near layers out before that, as the last line does. Put every depth in vh, not px, or the scene changes with the aspect. Give the camera a sideways drift of a few vw so the parallax shows in two axes. Keep the title the only large bright thing; the cards are context and stay dim. No blur is needed, the speed differences carry the depth.

Layered depth on a 2D camera move. When the move is a push, pull or whip on a flat world (see camera-moves) and it should read as a space, split the world into full-frame position: absolute; inset: 0 layers by depth and let the parallax helper scale each by its depth d (a push to 1.12 becomes 1.036 for the ground and 1.216 for the front):

js
import { parallax } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
parallax([[ground, 0.3], [mid, 1], [front, 1.8]], { kind: 'push', at: 0, duration: 2.4 });
parallax([[ground, 0.4], [far, 0.7], [mid, 1]], { kind: 'pull', at: 2.9, duration: 1.4, from: 1.15 });

The ground moves least, the type moves as the camera, a card or chip in front moves most. Keep the front layer's things inside the frame at the end of the move: at 1.8 a chip near the right edge leaves it. If the whole world also flies (scale-through), put the layers under one wrapper and fly the wrapper, because transforms on different elements compose.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: exposure-flash
moves.title: Exposure flash
moves.use: a cut on a screen film reads as over-exposure: 3 frames of white, the swap inside the peak, the new shot starts at 2x brightness and settles in 0.15 s; at most 3 flashes a second
moves.useWhen: a film cuts between worlds and the cut must read as a camera over-exposing: the frame blows out for 3 frames, the shot swaps inside the peak, and the new shot starts over-bright and settles in 0.15 s. A 0.3 s white div at partial opacity is not this: it is a fade, not a flash. The clip cuts between three photographs, each with a caption, a slow push and a running timecode.
moves.sound: a recorded hit at each cut, or one soft swell that stops dead on the cut (the film's one swell, on one flash only).
moves.snippet:
...
...
moves.useHtml: Use when a film cuts between worlds and the cut must read as a camera over-exposing: the frame blows out for 3 frames, the shot swaps inside the peak, and the new shot starts over-bright and settles in 0.15 s. A 0.3 s white div at partial opacity is not this: it is a fade, not a flash. The clip cuts between three photographs, each with a caption, a slow push and a running timecode.
moves.codeHtml:
html
<div id="host"><div class="shot">...</div><div class="shot">...</div></div>
<div id="white" style="position:absolute;inset:0;background:#fff;opacity:0"></div>
<script type="module">
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
import { flashAt } from '../../core/motion/exposure.js';
const CUTS = [1.4, 2.9];
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const { white: w, brightness, shot } = flashAt(t, CUTS);   // { fps: 30, frames: 3, peak: 0.75, over: 2, settle: 0.15 }
  shots.forEach((s, i) => s.toggleAttribute('data-on', i === shot));
  host.style.filter = brightness === 1 ? 'none' : `brightness(${brightness})`;
  white.style.opacity = w;
});
</script>
moves.soundHtml: Sound: a recorded hit at each cut, or one soft swell that stops dead on the cut (the film's one swell, on one flash only).
moves.notesHtml:
• The peak is frames / fps seconds centred on the cut: white at 0.75 alpha lifts a mean luma of 60 to about 200. shot counts the cuts passed, so the swap happens in the middle of the peak and the viewer never sees it.
  • After the peak the shot is at brightness(2) and eases to 1 on a squared curve over settle s. This is the falloff that makes it read as light.
  • flashAt flashes at most 3 cuts in any one second (flashCuts). A fourth cut in that second still cuts, without the flash. Keep flashes to a few per film; they are accents.
  • Use it once or twice a film, on the strongest beats only. Held for 6 frames or more it is a strobe.
  • Each shot has a slow push (EASE.glide, 6 percent) up to its cut, so the last frame before a flash is not a still. The timecode keeps the hold alive.
  • The renderer flags an all-white frame: declare it with <meta name="blank" content="1.35-1.45">.

Common mistake: three flat colour slates with a white fade between them. The shots must be real pictures with detail, so the viewer sees the highlights blow out and the detail return.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: lens
moves.title: Lens
moves.use: a screen filmed as a real object: tilt, depth, bloom, LED grid, fringes, done as lens work and never faked with CSS layers
moves.useWhen: a screen (a terminal, a dashboard, a tracking HUD, a type line shown as a monitor) must read as a real object filmed by a camera: tilted, soft at one end, bright glyphs blooming, LED cells and colour fringes visible when the camera pushes in. Render the flat screen, then let one shader film it.
moves.sound: a short noise tick at each tear, and a low thud on a lock (aberration peak). The lens itself is silent.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a screen (a terminal, a dashboard, a tracking HUD, a type line shown as a monitor) must read as a real object filmed by a camera: tilted, soft at one end, bright glyphs blooming, LED cells and colour fringes visible when the camera pushes in. Render the flat screen, then let one shader film it.

The six stages of the clip, each turned on for one second: flat, perspective, depth of field, palette and aberration, bloom and LED grid, tear and grain with the camera tracker.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { lens, htmlSource, PALETTES, OFF } from '/core/surfaces/lens.js';
const cam = lens(htmlSource(document.getElementById('screen'), { scale: 2 }), {
  aim: (t) => [1390, 520], zoom: (t) => 1 + 1.9 * ease(t), tiltY: 0.38, tiltX: 0.1,
  dof: { blur: 0.55, focus: [1400, 520] },
  palette: { stops: PALETTES.thermal, keepColor: 0.9 },
  bloom: { strength: 0.9, radius: 42 }, grid: { amount: 0.9, cell: 3 },
  aberration: { amount: (t) => 6 + 8 * lock(t) },
  tear: { amount: (t) => (hit(t) ? 70 : 0) },
});
vawe.onFrame((t) => cam.draw(t));            // the seek awaits it
const p = cam.project(1498, 440, t);         // { x, y, scale, depth, visible } in CSS px: put a label there
moves.soundHtml: Sound: a short noise tick at each tear, and a low thud on a lock (aberration peak). The lens itself is silent.
moves.notesHtml:
What it does

  • The screen is #screen: plain HTML and CSS, 1920 by 1080 px, parked behind the lens canvas. htmlSource inlines its computed styles and fonts into an SVG image and uploads it every seek. canvasSource(canvas) takes a 2D canvas instead.
  • Every option is a literal the page can change: a number, an array, or a function of the seek time. The defaults are the "filmed screen" look; OFF flattens every effect so one can be turned on alone.
  • perspective: tiltX, tiltY, roll, zoom (up to about 3), aim (the source point at the middle). A ray hits a tilted plane, so the far side is smaller and softer by geometry, not by a CSS skew.
  • dof: blur grows with the depth difference to focus (a source point: pass a function to follow a target). Bokeh takes the aperture's shape: blades (n-gon), rotation, roundness, and catEye squeezes it toward the frame edge. Bright pixels weigh more in the taps. soft is the lens floor. A source with a depth input (below) blurs by each pixel's own depth instead of the tilted plane.
  • palette: brightness through 2 to 8 colour stops (PALETTES.thermal phosphor amber navy paper mono cyanotype). keepColor leaves saturated marks (a red lock box) in their own colour.
  • Light is linear from the first tap to the last pass. grid is a panel mask on the screen plane: a soft dot per subpixel (layout stripe, triad or dot, softness), the same shape per channel so the average colour stays untinted. It follows the plane (period changes with zoom and tilt), fades out of focus, and is applied before bloom, so bright dots bleed into each other.
  • bloom: soft-knee threshold, then a 6-level downsample and upsample chain weighted by radius: a tight core plus a wide tail. aberration: red and blue move apart radially, amount px at the edge.
  • halation: the warm halo film gets where a bright edge meets dark. Pixels above threshold (0.6) go through the same blur chain as bloom at a wider radius (90 px), are multiplied by tint (default [1, 0.3, 0.1], a red-orange; pass [0.1, 0.4, 1] for a cold halo) and added only where the base is dark, so bright areas keep their colour. strength is 0 by default and in OFF: turn it on with about 0.5 to 1.2.
  • PALETTES.cyanotype: six stops measured from a reference image, dark to light: #010306 #070d13 #162432 #3b4f64 #6f8599 #ccd8e4. A near-black blue ground with a pale blue-grey top.
  • Optical effects, all off by default and in OFF (strength, amount or blur 0). Each one reads like a lens part: - streaks: { strength, length, threshold, tint }: anamorphic streaks. Pixels above threshold (0.7) go through the same blur chain as bloom, but the chain halves only the width, so a bright point becomes a thin horizontal line length px long (600), multiplied by tint (default blue) and added. Use about 0.3 to 1. - diffusion: { strength, radius }: Pro-Mist. A low-threshold wide glow (radius 70 px) added over the whole image, plus a very small black lift, so the blacks beside bright areas rise. Use about 0.2 to 0.5. - softFocus: { amount, radius }: the image mixed with a blurred copy of itself (radius 16 px). The core stays, the detail softens. Use amount 0.2 to 0.6. - tiltShift: { center, width, blur }: a sharp band (center and width are shares of the view height) with blur rising above and below it to blur px. It uses the circle-of-confusion path of dof, with the screen row as a synthetic depth. A source with its own depth keeps that depth and gets the band blur as a floor. - distortion: { amount }: a radial remap of the sample point. Above 0 is barrel (corners pulled in), below 0 is pincushion. Use -0.12 to 0.12. project() and quad() follow it. - weave: { amount }: gate weave. The whole image moves by up to amount px, a new seeded offset every frame (seed, fps). project() follows it.
  • tear (rows slide, seeded), grain, vignette, exposure, lift, fade. All noise is hashed from seed and floor(t * fps): a frame is a pure function of t, so renders match byte for byte.
  • project(x, y, t) is the same camera on the CPU. Labels, links and brackets drawn in HTML on top of the canvas (z-index above 0) stay sharp and show real source coordinates.

The numbers

The demo was measured against a reference, 1080p: bloom 90 to 10 percent width 24.9 px (reference 20.7), panel period 6.9 px (reference 7.1), colour fringe 35 percent of edges off by 1 px or more (reference 20 to 28). At 1080p a frame costs about 17 ms on the GPU (12 ms in a draft), and a 6 s final (360 frames) captures in about 20 s.

Looks

A look is a named set of lens options, data in LOOKS (core/surfaces/lens.js, next to PALETTES). lens(source, { look: 'film-halation', ...own }) starts from a flat lens, switches on the look, then puts the page's own options over it: a page option always wins. A page with no look keeps the filmed-screen defaults. Choose by sight: bin/vawe frames <page> --looks --at 4.5,9 [--only a,b] [--out dir] films the page frame at each second under every look and as-is, and writes one labelled grid per second (draft size, so a fine grid cell shows only in a final). The verb sets window.__vaweLensOverride before the page runs. lens() merges it over the page options, and it holds a full look: every effect the look does not name is off, while aim, zoom, tilt and dof stay the page's. Only the verb sets it.

| look | what it does | numbers | |---|---|---| | clean | every effect off: the flat screen with the page's camera | none | | dream-bloom | a wide, strong glow and a little soft focus | bloom 1.5, radius 120, threshold 0.22; softFocus 0.18, radius 30; vignette 0.15; lift 0.01 | | film-halation | the red-orange halo of film around bright edges | halation 1, radius 90, threshold 0.55; bloom 0.35; grain 0.05; vignette 0.25 | | anamorphic | blue horizontal streaks off bright shapes, a slight colour fringe | streaks 0.9, length 800, threshold 0.45, tint [0.35, 0.6, 1]; bloom 0.3; aberration 3; vignette 0.2 | | pro-mist | a soft veil: glow over the whole image and lifted blacks | diffusion 0.35, radius 70; vignette 0.1 | | tilt-shift | a sharp middle band, blur above and below | tiltShift center 0.5, width 0.3, blur 22 | | soft-focus | the whole image mixed half with a blurred copy | softFocus 0.5, radius 14 | | vintage | warm tone, grain, weave, strong vignette, soft halo | palette warm 4 stops at 0.4; halation 0.5; bloom 0.3; grain 0.09; weave 1.6; vignette 0.55; lift 0.02 | | cyanotype | the cyanotype palette, a cold halo, grain | PALETTES.cyanotype; halation 0.8, tint [0.1, 0.4, 1]; grain 0.07; vignette 0.3 | | crt | LED stripe grid, torn rows, colour fringe, strong bloom | grid 0.9, cell 3; tear 6, prob 0.04; aberration 5; bloom 0.7; vignette 0.5; grain 0.04 |

Depth of field for a 3D scene

A tilted plane gives depth by geometry. A three.js scene has depth per pixel, so give the lens that depth: canvasSource(color, { depth }). depth is a canvas (or ImageBitmap, ImageData) holding linear depth in the red channel, 0 near to 1 far, or a function returning one, called on every draw. It may have another size than the colour canvas. The circle of confusion is blur x |depth - focus|, so dof.focus is a depth number (0 to 1; a function of t racks it) or a source point whose depth is read. max, bokeh, blades, soft keep their meaning. A sharp near object does not smear into the blurred far one; a blurred near object spreads over the far one. Without depth the plane path runs unchanged. Depth is 8 bit here: avoid a range wider than the scene needs.

js
const color = Object.assign(document.createElement('canvas'), { width: 1920, height: 1080 });
const depth = Object.assign(document.createElement('canvas'), { width: 1920, height: 1080 });
const depthMat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({   // linear view depth, not the nonlinear depth buffer
  uniforms: { near: { value: camera.near }, far: { value: camera.far } },
  vertexShader: 'varying float v; void main() { vec4 m = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0); v = -m.z; gl_Position = projectionMatrix * m; }',
  fragmentShader: 'uniform float near, far; varying float v; void main() { gl_FragColor = vec4(vec3(clamp((v - near) / (far - near), 0.0, 1.0)), 1.0); }',
});
function renderBoth(t) {
  scene.background = beautyBackground; scene.overrideMaterial = null;
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
  color.getContext('2d').drawImage(renderer.domElement, 0, 0);
  scene.background = new THREE.Color(1, 1, 1); scene.overrideMaterial = depthMat;   // far = white
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
  depth.getContext('2d').drawImage(renderer.domElement, 0, 0);
  scene.overrideMaterial = null;
}
const cam = lens(canvasSource(color, { depth }), { dof: { blur: 0.6, focus: (t) => rack(t) } });   // rack: depth 0..1
vawe.onFrame(async (t) => { update(t); renderBoth(t); await cam.draw(t); });

Set the renderer's preserveDrawingBuffer: true or copy right after each render, as above. Lights and fog do not touch the override material, so the depth stays a pure function of the geometry.

Rejected approximations

These faked one effect per element and never matched a camera:

  • text-shadow or filter: drop-shadow as bloom: the glow follows the glyph shape, ignores the rest of the frame, and cannot be lifted by what sits next to it. Use bloom.
  • A repeating-gradient overlay as the pixel grid: it does not follow perspective, does not fade out of focus and tints the average colour. Use grid.
  • One filter: blur() as depth of field: a uniform blur has no depth. Use dof over a tilted plane.
  • Depth bands by screen height as the depth of a 3D scene: a subject that crosses a band gets the wrong blur. Pass depth to canvasSource.
  • CSS transform: perspective() rotate3d() on the screen: a skew of the layer, one blur per plane, sharp text on the far side. Use tiltX, tiltY and zoom.
  • mix-blend-mode colour layers as a palette: use palette.

Views and movements (product shot)

core/surfaces/lens-views.js holds the presets of a product shot as data and pure helpers, so a page names a view instead of writing angles. Angles are degrees as CSS reads them; lensPose(pose) gives tiltX, tiltY, roll, zoom. The numbers come from a measured study of a product-shot tool (its four perspective presets, and its screen movement ranges with its clamp of 25 degrees on rotateX and rotateY); the source is recorded at the top of the file.

js
import { view, viewScaled, lensPose, moveBetween, backdropFor, shadowFor } from '/core/surfaces/lens-views.js';
const orbit = moveBetween('soft-orbit', 3, { scale: 0.6 });   // { from, to } poses, seeded, x and y clamped to 25 degrees
const away = viewScaled('reverse-isometric', 0.5);            // 10 and 22.5 degrees
const backdrop = backdropFor(pageEdgeRgb);                    // the page's edge colour, a little lighter on a dark page
const cue = shadowFor(backdrop, pageEdgeRgb);                 // layers, rim light and reflection that read on that backdrop
  • Views: flat, side-angle, isometric, top-diagonal, reverse-isometric. Movements: soft-orbit, side-drift, focus-push, focus-pull, diagonal-rise, angle-settle, close-orbit, wide-sweep, isometric-glide, isometric-reveal. The same name and seed give the same move.
  • shadowFor: a light backdrop (luminance 0.18 or more) gets the plain soft shadow. A dark one swallows it, so it gets layers of alpha 0.7 and 0.85, a rim light on the page edge (alpha 0.3) and a faint reflection (alpha 0.07). Draw them in the page; lens does not. Before you pick a backdrop, make 3 options and compare them in one vawe sheet.
  • Keep text readable: reading poses stay within 10 degrees, a start within about 15. Put the lens dof.focus on what the viewer must read (a function of t) and push zoom and aim to it; keep dof.blur near 0.45 so only the far edge softens.
  • A real screen keeps the real-surface rule: the plane and the camera move, the page moves only as it does.

Never lose the screen

A tilted plane can swing its border into the frame or turn away from the target. edge: 'extend' (the default) repeats the screen's edge pixels past the border; edge: 'black' shows outside. fit moves the camera instead: fit: { keep: [x, y], margin: 80 } pans (then zooms out) until the point holds inside the frame, and cover: true until no border shows. cam.project(x, y, t).visible and cam.quad(t) (the four screen corners in CSS px) let a check warn when a shot loses its target.

Limits

htmlSource needs everything inside the screen to be self-contained: fonts from the page's @font-face, images and url() backgrounds are inlined; <video>, <iframe> and CSS counters are not carried. Set scale: 2 when zoom goes above 1.5, or small text turns soft. A page with a lens needs WebGL2.

moves.name: camera-moves
moves.title: Camera moves
moves.use: a whole world as one wrapper: push toward a subject (the ground scales less so the layers separate), pull, whip between worlds (camera()); the camera holds still by default
moves.useWhen: a whole world should feel like it is seen through a lens that moves: lean in on a hold, pull back to reveal, whip to the next world. The clip runs a push over a real product page (a browser window with a dashboard). The window is the subject, a fine grid is the ground behind it, and a hover tooltip floats in front. The three layers scale by different amounts, so they separate the way real depth does. Each move is a transform on one wrapper (or on one layer, see the layered depth section of parallax-dive), so it is deterministic under the seek.
moves.sound: a whoosh at the start of a whip, one per film; the push, pull and drift are felt, not heard.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a whole world should feel like it is seen through a lens that moves: lean in on a hold, pull back to reveal, whip to the next world. The clip runs a push over a real product page (a browser window with a dashboard). The window is the subject, a fine grid is the ground behind it, and a hover tooltip floats in front. The three layers scale by different amounts, so they separate the way real depth does. Each move is a transform on one wrapper (or on one layer, see the layered depth section of parallax-dive), so it is deterministic under the seek.

The camera holds still by default. It moves only with a reason: the spectacle, a reveal. A camera that moves in every beat is the lazy way to keep a hold alive. The taste rule constant-camera names a camera that moves for over 60 percent of the film or over 4 worlds in a row.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { camera, EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const w = document.querySelector('[data-world="hero"]');
camera(w, { kind: 'push', at: 0, duration: 2.4, origin: '66% 56%' });      // 1 to 1.12, EASE.glide: never quite stops
camera(w, { kind: 'pull', at: 0, duration: 1.4 });                          // 1.15 to 1, EASE.settle: reveals
camera(oldWorld, { kind: 'whipOut', at: 5.0, duration: 0.3 });             // the old world leaves on EASE.launch
camera(newWorld, { kind: 'whipIn', at: 5.0, duration: 0.3 });              // the new one arrives on EASE.land
moves.soundHtml: Sound: a whoosh at the start of a whip, one per film; the push, pull and drift are felt, not heard.
moves.notesHtml:
Push toward a subject. Scale the world toward the subject, not the frame centre. Scale the ground less and the part in front more. The demo pushes 2.6 s on EASE.glide:

js
const S = { ground: 1.04, world: 1.14, front: 1.2 };
[['#grid', S.ground], ['#world', S.world], ['#front', S.front]].forEach(([sel, to]) => {
  const el = document.querySelector(sel);
  el.style.transformOrigin = `${O.x}px ${O.y}px`;                           // one origin for all three layers
  el.animate([{ scale: 1 }, { scale: to }], { duration: 2600, delay: 900, easing: EASE.glide, fill: 'both' });
});
// a part on the front layer lands on its target after both layers scale: place it at O + (target - O) * S.world / S.front

Push 8 to 20 percent over the beat. Under 5 percent the eye reads a mistake. Over 30 percent it is a punch-in (crash-zoom) and needs a faster curve. A camera move under 2 s takes EASE.land. A move of 2 s or more takes EASE.glide, which keeps the lean going to the last frame. End the push before the hold, and keep the hold alive with a part that moves (here a hover that steps from one bar to the next), never a camera drift. Never blur a push: the subject is the sharpest thing in frame.

Common mistake: one scale on a flat card over a flat ground. Nothing separates, so the push reads as a zoom. Give the move a real page, a ground that scales less and a part in front that scales more.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: depth-resolve
moves.title: Depth resolve
moves.use: far words small and soft resolve as the camera arrives; a focus pull (focus())
moves.useWhen: a line has two depths: the words that matter are near and sharp, the words around them are far, small and soft, and they resolve as the camera arrives. The same call is a focus pull on any element: a blur that clears. It guides the eye (near first, far second) and makes a held frame richer.
moves.sound: none.
moves.useHtml: Use when a line has two depths: the words that matter are near and sharp, the words around them are far, small and soft, and they resolve as the camera arrives. The same call is a focus pull on any element: a blur that clears. It guides the eye (near first, far second) and makes a held frame richer.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { focus, parallax, stagger } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const far = document.querySelectorAll('.far');          // small, soft ink, e.g. 7% of frame height
parallax([[ground, 0.4], [farLayer, 0.7], [mid, 1]], { kind: 'pull', at: 2.9, duration: 1.4, from: 1.15 });
stagger(document.querySelectorAll('.near'), { at: 3.0, band: 'professional', from: '0 0.5em' });
far.forEach((el, i) => focus(el, { at: 3.5 + i * 0.12, blur: 9, scale: 0.8, opacity: 0.4, duration: 0.9 }));
// a plain focus pull: focus(card, { at: 1, blur: 14 })
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none.
moves.notesHtml: focus clears blur px from a smaller (scale) and fainter (opacity) start on EASE.settle, which never overshoots; the far words settle after the near ones, 0.1 s apart, ending as the camera stops. Far words rest at an ink with 4.5:1 contrast on the ground (the dev check reads the pixels), so do not fade them to a ghost: depth is size and softness, not low contrast. Keep far text off the near text's box. See also rack-focus for a focus that shifts between two subjects.

moves.name: scale-through
moves.title: Scale through
moves.use: fly into a plain element and its colour is the next world, in Web Animations only
moves.useWhen: the next world should be entered, not cut to: the camera flies into one plain element (a dot, a disc) until it fills the frame, and its colour is the ground of the next world. Pure Web Animations, no per-frame code; for the zoom-blur fan of copies see zoom-through.
moves.sound: a rising whoosh over the dive, a soft hit at the swap.
moves.useHtml: Use when the next world should be entered, not cut to: the camera flies into one plain element (a dot, a disc) until it fills the frame, and its colour is the ground of the next world. Pure Web Animations, no per-frame code; for the zoom-blur fan of copies see zoom-through.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
const STOPS = 16, SCALE = 26;                       // disc of radius r fills the frame corner at about corner / r
const a = document.querySelector('[data-world="a"]');
a.style.transformOrigin = '67.9% 56.7%';            // the disc's centre as it rests, after any push
// log-spaced stops: equal steps in zoom feel even; the easing runs over the whole move
a.animate(Array.from({ length: STOPS + 1 }, (_, i) => ({ scale: String(SCALE ** (i / STOPS)) })),
  { delay: 2400, duration: 700, easing: EASE.launch, fill: 'both' });
// world a hides the moment the disc fills the frame; world b (ground = the disc's colour) sits under it
a.animate([{ opacity: 1 }, { opacity: 0 }], { delay: 3060, duration: 1, fill: 'forwards' });
moves.soundHtml: Sound: a rising whoosh over the dive, a soft hit at the swap.
moves.notesHtml: The disc must be a flat colour with no glyph and the next world's ground must be that colour, or the swap shows. EASE.launch accelerates to the cut; the swap frame is one frame of flat colour, so start the next world's words 0.1 s before it hides the old one. Linear scale between two keys feels slow then sudden: the log-spaced stops fix that. Never push in the same direction twice in a row: follow a scale-through with a pull back or a whip (taste rule seam-variety).

moves.name: direction-wipe
moves.title: Direction wipe
moves.use: a mask edge moves the way the last move went and reveals the next beat
moves.useWhen: the thing on screen moves and the next beat should arrive along the same line: a bar sweeping right wipes in the next world from the left edge of its path, so the cut reads as the movement continuing. A fade or a wipe against the movement reads as a second event.
moves.sound: a short swipe, timed to the edge's fastest frame.
moves.useHtml: Use when the thing on screen moves and the next beat should arrive along the same line: a bar sweeping right wipes in the next world from the left edge of its path, so the cut reads as the movement continuing. A fade or a wipe against the movement reads as a second event.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
// the old world's motion ends moving right; the next world is revealed by a mask edge that moves right too
const next = document.querySelector('[data-world="b"]');
next.style.clipPath = 'inset(0 100% 0 0)';
next.animate([{ clipPath: 'inset(0 100% 0 0)' }, { clipPath: 'inset(0 0% 0 0)' }],
  { delay: 2000, duration: 450, easing: EASE.carry, fill: 'both' });
// the leading edge carries a thin line of the accent so the eye sees what moved
edge.animate([{ left: '0%' }, { left: '100%' }], { delay: 2000, duration: 450, easing: EASE.carry, fill: 'both' });
moves.soundHtml: Sound: a short swipe, timed to the edge's fastest frame.
moves.notesHtml: Match the axis and direction of the last visible move: a rise wipes up (inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0)), a slide left wipes from the right. EASE.carry is still fast at the end, so the wipe hands its speed to the next beat's first move (start that move 60 ms before the wipe ends). Change the direction at the next seam (taste rule seam-variety). For a coloured edge see color-block-wipe.

moves.name: arrival-spring
moves.title: Arrival spring
moves.use: EASE.nudge on one arrival in three, EASE.pop on the one that matters (nudgeEvery)
moves.useWhen: a film has many arrivals and every one lands on the same soft stop. The reference films overshoot 21 to 41 percent of their arrivals; a film where none do reads stiff. EASE.nudge passes its mark by about 6 per cent and settles back: enough to read as alive, small enough for type. EASE.pop passes by 15 per cent and is for the one arrival that is the point (a CTA, a check, the hero word).
moves.sound: a soft tick on each overshooting arrival is enough; none on the rest.

EASE.nudge passes its mark by about 6 per cent and settles back: enough to read as alive, small enough for type. EASE.pop passes by 15 per cent and is for the one arrival that is the point (a CTA, a check, the hero word).
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { enter, stagger, EASE } from '../../core/motion/presets.js';
// every 3rd word of the line lands on EASE.nudge, the rest on EASE.land
stagger(document.querySelectorAll('.line .w'), { at: 0.2, band: 'professional', from: '0 0.5em', nudgeEvery: 3 });
// the one arrival that matters: a deeper spring
enter(document.querySelector('.hero'), { at: 1.2, duration: 0.7, scale: 0.7, ease: 'pop' });
moves.soundHtml: Sound: a soft tick on each overshooting arrival is enough; none on the rest.
moves.notesHtml: Pick the springs, do not spread them: one arrival in three (21 to 41 percent of the film) on nudge, at most one or two on pop, the rest on land. Put the spring on the arrival the eye is on, not on the ground. A scene may use two eases (land and nudge); a third (pop) counts as one more, so use pop on the spectacle beat only. The dev check overshoot-share counts an arrival as overshooting when its easing peaks above 1.01, so nudge (peak 1.06) and pop (1.15) are both counted. A move under 20 px has no room to overshoot by a pixel: give the spring to the larger moves.

moves.name: rack-focus
moves.title: Rack focus
moves.use: focus moves from one depth layer to another: near melts, far resolves, pinpoint lights swell into discs; use once per film
moves.useWhen: two things at different depths share a frame and the story passes from one to the other: the draft in front, the shipped result behind. The lens pulls focus: one plane resolves while the others go soft.
moves.sound: none; a focus pull is felt, never heard.
moves.useHtml:
Use when two things at different depths share a frame and the story passes from one to the other: the draft in front, the shipped result behind. The lens pulls focus: one plane resolves while the others go soft.

Look: a real photo as the far plane, always soft, with two pale paper cards over it at two depths (0.2 and 0.55; the photo sits at 0.95). The cards are drawn on a 2D canvas with a soft contact shadow, a mono label, a large word and a status line. Each card is sharp only when the focus is on its depth.

How it moves: the cards arrive on EASE.land (a 0.4 s fade with a 14 px rise, 150 ms apart). Focus sits on the near card for 1.2 s, then moves to the second card in 1.0 s on EASE.settle: the near card melts, the second resolves. Focus holds, then the cards leave on EASE.launch. The soft parts are a true depth of field: the circle of confusion grows with the depth difference, so the card next to the photo is less soft than the photo.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { lens, canvasSource, OFF } from '/core/surfaces/lens.js';
const NEAR = 0.2, MID = 0.55, FAR = 0.95;                         // depth, 0 near to 1 far
const rack = (t) => NEAR + (MID - NEAR) * easeFn('settle')(clamp((t - 1.2) / 1.0));
// paint(t) draws the photo and the cards into `color`, and each shape in its depth grey into `depth` (red channel)
const cam = lens(canvasSource(color, { depth }), { ...OFF, dof: { blur: 0.9, focus: rack, bokeh: 8 } });
vawe.onFrame(async (t) => { paint(t); await cam.draw(t); });
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; a focus pull is felt, never heard.
moves.notesHtml:
Common mistake: two filter: blur() layers swapped on one curve. A uniform blur has no depth, so the plane between them never shows. Give each shape a depth and let the lens dof blur by distance from the focus.

moves.name: drift-hold
moves.title: Drift hold
moves.use: the line holds still while only the ground drifts, so a held frame never sits dead
moves.useWhen: one line must sit still on screen long enough to read and you want a living ground behind it as a deliberate option. The line never moves; only the ground behind it drifts, slowly, like a breath. This is a ground option, not the hold's life: a ground drift does not keep a hold alive (rule live-hold), so the held seconds still need an element motion on a part of the frame.
moves.sound: none; a hold is quiet, and the quiet before the spectacle is the point.
moves.snippet: Held, not frozen.

moves.codeHtml:
html
<div class="ground"></div>                         <!-- inset: -8%, a dot grid or a texture -->
<div class="light"></div>                          <!-- one soft radial patch, lighter than the ground -->
<h1 class="line">Held, not <em>frozen.</em></h1>   <!-- no transform, ever -->
<script type="module">
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
import { noise1 } from '../../core/motion/springs.js';
const layers = [
  { el: ground, seed: 1, amp: 1.6, grow: 0.03 },   // vh of travel, share of scale gained over 2 s
  { el: light,  seed: 2, amp: 5,   grow: 0.06 },
];
const rate = 0.5;                                  // noise steps per second: a new direction every 2 s
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const vh = innerHeight / 100;
  layers.forEach(({ el, seed, amp, grow }) => {
    const x = noise1(t * rate, seed * 10) * amp * vh, y = noise1(t * rate, seed * 10 + 5) * amp * vh * 0.7;
    el.style.transform = `translate(${x}px, ${y}px) scale(${1 + grow * t / 2})`;
  });
});
</script>
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; a hold is quiet, and the quiet before the spectacle is the point.
moves.notesHtml:
The ground drift is the ground's life (rule living-ground). It is a whole-frame move, so it does not count for live-hold: give the held line's seconds an element motion too (a glint, a caret, a counter).

noise1 is seeded, so frame t is the same on every render and depends on no earlier frame. Put the drift only on layers behind the text: the moment the line itself drifts, the eye reads a move and not a hold. The grid travels 1 to 2 vh; the light patch may travel more because its edge is soft. Keep the patch within a few percent of the ground's lightness, so it reads as light and not as a shape. It never blurs. Use it under a held line, not as a substitute for a beat: the hold still needs its own words-times-0.6 s.

moves.name: gradient-mesh-field
moves.title: Gradient mesh field
moves.use: a title sits on a living ground: four soft colour pools drift on seeded paths in one fragment shader, with grain against banding; the copy keeps 4.5:1
moves.useWhen: a title and one line sit on a ground that must visibly flow, as on a modern product hero. The clip is five layers of warm colour with crisp edges, drawn on a canvas. Each edge is a sine curve with its own phase and speed, so the layers drift across the frame and never cross. The colour fades to the flat ground on the left, under the copy, and reaches full strength on the right. One thin darker sand layer widens once, at 1.6 s. Each edge has a 1 px highlight and a soft contact shadow, as layers of paper have. The copy enters with a masked rise and a blur cascade.
moves.sound: none; a held ground is quiet, and a pad under it reads as a screensaver.

Each edge is a sine curve with its own phase and speed, so the layers drift across the frame and never cross. The colour fades to the flat ground on the left, under the copy, and reaches full strength on the right. One thin darker sand layer widens once, at 1.6 s. moves.codeHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
const LAYERS = [   // top to bottom: base height, amplitude, waves across the frame, phase, speed (rad/s), colour
  { y: 0.10, a: 0.045, f: 1.0, p: 0.0, w: 1.1, c: '#eee6d6' },
  { y: 0.52, a: 0.040, f: 1.2, p: 4.4, w: 1.3, c: '#a8855a' },   // the darker sand layer: it widens once
  // ...three more layers in the demo
];
const edge = (L, x, t, extra) => H * (L.y + extra + (x / W - 0.5) * 0.2 + L.a * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * L.f * x / W + L.p + L.w * t));
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  ctx.fillStyle = ground; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  LAYERS.forEach((L, i) => {
    // fill from the edge down to the bottom with a horizontal gradient: ground at the left, full colour at the right
    ctx.shadowColor = 'rgba(70, 45, 20, 0.2)'; ctx.shadowBlur = 2.4 * u; ctx.shadowOffsetY = -0.7 * u;   // a contact shadow above the edge
    ctx.fillStyle = gradientOf(L); fill(path(L, t));
    ctx.shadowColor = 'transparent'; ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)'; stroke(path(L, t));   // the highlight
  });
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; a held ground is quiet, and a pad under it reads as a screensaver.
moves.notesHtml:
The time is the seek, so every render draws the same layers. Sine edges with a spacing larger than twice the amplitude never cross. Keep the colours inside one warm family and stay on one sand ramp. Behind the copy the layers are within a few percent of the ground, so the headline keeps its contrast. Every layer fades from the ground with the same gradient: a layer that starts at a set x shows a vertical seam.

Common mistake: soft blurred pools of colour. A mesh that reads as a modern ground has crisp edges and flat colour inside each layer. The flow comes from the edges moving, not from a blur.

moves.name: pan-stations
moves.title: Pan stations
moves.use: several steps or features as one continuous place: the camera pans between stations on one wide canvas and holds at each, a rail and a parallax dot grid carrying the space between them
moves.useWhen: three to six steps or features should read as one continuous place, with no cuts: they sit on one wide canvas, and the camera pans from station to station and holds at each. The detail that sells the space is what lies between the stations: a dashed rail runs node to node under the cards and past both ends, a dot grid behind moves at 55 percent of the camera (parallax), and each node lights as the camera arrives. Without them the pans read as slides pushed sideways.
moves.sound: pluck at 0.92 s and at 1.62 s into the move, when each node lights on the camera's arrival (default gain); nothing on the pans.

The detail that sells the space is what lies between the stations: a dashed rail runs node to node under the cards and past both ends, a dot grid behind moves at 55 percent of the camera (parallax), and each node lights as the camera arrives. Without them the pans read as slides pushed sideways.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
const vw = innerWidth / 100, vh = innerHeight / 100;
const at = [{ x: 50, y: 50 }, { x: 150, y: 58 }, { x: 250, y: 44 }];   // station centres on the canvas, vw and vh
const PANS = [0.5, 1.2], PAN = 0.42, DRIFT = 0.8;                       // pan starts (s), pan length (s), drift (vw per s)
const inout = easeFn('settle');                // no jolt at either end
const clamp = (u) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, u));
const cam = (t) => {
  let k = 0;
  PANS.forEach((s) => { k += inout(clamp((t - s) / PAN)); });           // k: 0 at station 1, 1 at station 2, ...
  const i = Math.min(at.length - 2, Math.floor(k)), f = k - i;
  return { x: at[i].x + (at[i + 1].x - at[i].x) * f + DRIFT * t, y: at[i].y + (at[i + 1].y - at[i].y) * f };
};
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  const c = cam(t), n = cam(t + 1 / 60);
  const tx = (50 - c.x) * vw, ty = (50 - c.y) * vh;
  world.style.transform = `translate(${tx}px, ${ty}px)`;
  far.style.transform = `translate(${tx * 0.55}px, ${ty * 0.55}px)`;
  blur.setAttribute('stdDeviation', `${Math.abs(n.x - c.x) * vw * 0.35} 0`);   // #motion feGaussianBlur on .world
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: pluck at 0.92 s and at 1.62 s into the move, when each node lights on the camera's arrival (default gain); nothing on the pans.
moves.notesHtml:
A pan of 0.42 s over one frame width is fast enough to feel like one space and slow enough to stay readable mid-pan; under 0.3 s it becomes a whip pan. Step the stations up and down a little so the pans are not one flat rail, and let the camera drift slowly through the holds so a held station is never a still. In a film, hold each station for its text (words x 0.6 s, at least 1.2 s); the demo holds shorter to show the move in 2 s.
