moves.name: ink-warp
moves.title: Ink warp
moves.use: a rich liquid ground for short large copy: marbled ink flows by domain warp in one shader, thinner behind the type
moves.useWhen: the frame wants a rich, liquid ground, like ink spreading in water, and the copy is short and large. One shader folds noise into itself (a domain warp): a body colour and a thin vein colour flow in marbled shapes, thinner behind the copy.
moves.sound: none; a held ground is quiet.
moves.useHtml: Use when the frame wants a rich, liquid ground, like ink spreading in water, and the copy is short and large. One shader folds noise into itself (a domain warp): a body colour and a thin vein colour flow in marbled shapes, thinner behind the copy.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
import { shaderField } from '../../core/surfaces/shader-field.js';
const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
const rgb = (name) => { const h = css.getPropertyValue(name).trim(); return [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16) / 255); };
const frag = `
uniform vec3 u_ground, u_ink, u_vein;
float hash(vec2 p) { return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(127.1, 311.7)) + u_seed * 17.0) * 43758.5453); }
float vnoise(vec2 p) {
  vec2 i = floor(p), f = fract(p); f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
  return mix(mix(hash(i), hash(i + vec2(1, 0)), f.x), mix(hash(i + vec2(0, 1)), hash(i + vec2(1, 1)), f.x), f.y);
}
float fbm(vec2 p) { float s = 0.0, a = 0.5; for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) { s += a * vnoise(p); p = p * 2.03 + 11.7; a *= 0.5; } return s; }
vec3 lin(vec3 c) { return pow(c, vec3(2.2)); }
void main() {
  float aspect = u_res.x / u_res.y;
  vec2 p = gl_FragCoord.xy / u_res.y;
  float t = u_time * 0.4;                                              // the one speed: time moves the warp, not the grid
  vec2 q = vec2(fbm(p * 1.6 + vec2(0.0, t)), fbm(p * 1.6 + vec2(5.2, 1.3 - t)));
  vec2 r = vec2(fbm(p * 1.6 + 3.0 * q + vec2(1.7, 9.2) + t * 0.7), fbm(p * 1.6 + 3.0 * q + vec2(8.3, 2.8) - t * 0.6));
  float n = fbm(p * 1.6 + 3.2 * r);                                    // noise of noise of noise: the marbling
  float body = smoothstep(0.35, 0.80, n);
  float vein = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.035, abs(n - 0.52));            // a thin line where n crosses 0.52
  float keep = 1.0 - 0.7 * smoothstep(0.86 * aspect, 0.50 * aspect, p.x);   // thin the ink behind the copy
  vec3 col = lin(u_ground) + lin(u_ink) * 0.42 * body * keep + lin(u_vein) * 0.16 * vein * keep * keep;
  gl_FragColor = vec4(pow(col, vec3(1.0 / 2.2)) + (hash(gl_FragCoord.xy) - 0.5) * 0.012, 1.0);   // static dither
}`;
const field = shaderField(frag, { seed: 4, uniforms: { u_ground: rgb('--ground'), u_ink: rgb('--tile-alt'), u_vein: rgb('--accent') } });
vawe.onFrame((t) => field.draw(t));
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; a held ground is quiet.
moves.notesHtml: Measured on the 4 s demo clip at 640 x 360 on the signal look (ground, --tile-alt violet body, mint accent veins): the mean luma change is 1.3 per frame at 60 fps, 1.1 once the copy has settled, and the worst contrast of white ink against the lightest pixel behind the text box is 10.9:1 over 12 frames. This is the busiest ground of the group, so it is the one to keep dim. The first render ran at t * 0.55 with ink at 0.55 and measured 2.2: close to the 3.0 ceiling and loud on the sheet, with the violet reading as a subject. Slowing to 0.4 and dimming the ink to 0.42 kept the marbling and took the change to 1.3. Use a body colour with no more luma than a mid purple; a mint body would break the 4.5:1 rule under white type. The veins are the brightest pixels, so they fade twice as fast as the body behind the copy (keep * keep). Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: dot-grid-wave
moves.title: Dot grid wave
moves.use: a clean product or data frame gets a plain SVG dot grid with one travelling wave of scale and brightness, weaker behind the copy
moves.useWhen: a clean product or data frame needs a ground that reads as a fine texture and shows a wave only when it passes. The clip is a flat neutral ground with a field of ink dots, 2.4 percent of the frame height apart. A band of larger, darker dots travels across the field on a diagonal, twice in 5 s. The dots behind the copy fade to 30 percent, so the title stays clean. The copy rises in a mask and the lead resolves word by word. It is SVG with the look's ink, no shader.
moves.sound: none; a held ground is quiet.
moves.useHtml: Use when a clean product or data frame needs a ground that reads as a fine texture and shows a wave only when it passes. The clip is a flat neutral ground with a field of ink dots, 2.4 percent of the frame height apart. A band of larger, darker dots travels across the field on a diagonal, twice in 5 s. The dots behind the copy fade to 30 percent, so the title stays clean. The copy rises in a mask and the lead resolves word by word. It is SVG with the look's ink, no shader.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import '../../core/engine/page-api.js';
const PITCH = 0.024, BASE = 0.0016, PEAK = 0.0036, PASSES = [0.5, 2.7], SPEED = 0.7, SIGMA = 0.15;   // radii and pitch: shares of the frame height
const W = innerWidth, H = innerHeight;
const dots = [];   // one <circle> per grid point; s is its place along the band's direction, keep fades it behind the copy
for (let y = PITCH * H / 2; y < H; y += PITCH * H) {
  for (let x = PITCH * H / 2; x < W; x += PITCH * H) {
    // ...create the circle at (x, y) in the <svg class="grid">...
    dots.push({ c, s: (x * 0.94 + y * 0.34) / W, keep });
  }
}
vawe.onFrame((t) => {
  for (const d of dots) {
    let w = 0;                                                    // the band is a bell curve that travels: a pure function of t
    for (const t0 of PASSES) { const e = (d.s - (-0.35 + (t - t0) * SPEED)) / SIGMA; w = Math.max(w, Math.exp(-e * e)); }
    d.c.setAttribute('r', (H * (BASE + (PEAK - BASE) * w)).toFixed(2));
    d.c.setAttribute('opacity', (d.keep * (0.2 + 0.7 * w)).toFixed(3));
  }
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; a held ground is quiet.
moves.notesHtml:
The dots are 1.2 px at rest and 2.6 px in the band on a 720 p frame, in the ink colour at 20 and 90 percent opacity. Smaller dots vanish in the encode, and dots in an accent colour read as decoration. The band is narrow (half-width 0.15 frame widths), so the eye sees a wave pass and then a quiet field. Both passes start off screen and end off screen, so the first and the last frame show the same resting grid.

Common mistake: moving cx or cy. A grid whose dots move reads as a swarm. Change only the radius and the opacity, and the grid stays a grid.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: light-pool
moves.title: Light pool
moves.use: a matte held frame gets one soft pool of light that wanders on a seeded path, plain CSS with no shader; the stillest ground of the group
moves.useWhen: a held, matte frame needs one slow event behind the type: a single soft key light that wanders over a lit surface.
moves.sound: none; a held ground is quiet.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a held, matte frame needs one slow event behind the type: a single soft key light that wanders over a lit surface.

Look: a warm grey wall of vertical ribs. Each rib has a bright left edge, a flat middle and a dark right edge. A second layer holds the same ribs in a lighter tone and shows only inside a soft round mask, so each rib lights where the pool is and stays dim elsewhere. A faint dark vignette sits over the wall. The type is dark ink and reads on both tones.

How it moves: the headline rises out of a mask on EASE.land and the lead fades up. The pool wanders on a seeded noise path (about 1.3 steps a second) and never stops. The copy leaves on leave; the wall and the light stay.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const RATE = 1.3, AMP_X = 0.36, AMP_Y = 0.26;                 // noise steps a second; travel as shares of the frame
vawe.onFrame((t) => {                                          // noise1 from core/motion/springs.js: frame t is the same on every render
  const W = innerWidth, H = innerHeight, mw = 1.2 * H, mh = 0.92 * H;   // the mask size
  lit.style.setProperty('--px', `${W * (0.52 + AMP_X * noise1(t * RATE, 11)) - mw / 2}px`);
  lit.style.setProperty('--py', `${H * (0.45 + AMP_Y * noise1(t * RATE, 23)) - mh / 2}px`);
});
// .lit: the bright ribs, mask-image: radial-gradient(closest-side, #000, transparent), mask-position: var(--px) var(--py)
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; a held ground is quiet.
moves.notesHtml:
Common mistake: a coloured radial glow drifting behind the type. It lights nothing and reads as a blob. Light a surface that has a form (ribs, plaster, fabric), and keep the light neutral and warm.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: marquee-along-path
moves.title: Marquee along path
moves.use: tiles ride one SVG path forever at an even gap, turned with the curve, rolling z-index, 8 percent of the path per second; one element along the path is an option
moves.useWhen: a row of things must travel a curve for a whole beat: a loop-the-loop of tiles, a ribbon of logos or posters, a stream that rides an S-curve behind a title. Every item sits on the same SVG path at an even gap and moves forever; the path can show or hide.
moves.sound: none; or one tick as the lead tile crosses the loop.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a row of things must travel a curve for a whole beat: a loop-the-loop of tiles, a ribbon of logos or posters, a stream that rides an S-curve behind a title. Every item sits on the same SVG path at an even gap and moves forever; the path can show or hide.

Credit: port of fancy by Daniel Petho, MIT. Source: marquee-along-svg-path and element-along-svg-path (repo). The maths and the demo path are the originals'.

Each item is a box with offset-path: path(...) and an offset-distance that the page sets from the time. offset-rotate stays at its default auto, so each tile turns with the curve and its centre sits on the path.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const BASE_VELOCITY = 8;            // percent of the path per second
const REPEAT = 2;                   // copies of the child list: 13 tiles x 2 = 26 items, 100/26 percent apart
const SCROLL_FACTOR = 5 / 1000;     // the original maps a constant 1 through [0, 1000] -> [0, 5]: speed x 1.005
const wrap = (v) => ((v % 100) + 100) % 100;
window.seek = (t) => items.forEach((el, i) => {
  const pct = wrap(BASE_VELOCITY * (1 + SCROLL_FACTOR) * t + (i * 100) / items.length);  // direction reverse: negate the first term
  el.style.offsetPath = `path('${PATH}')`;                                              // viewBox px, same box as the svg
  el.style.offsetDistance = `${easing ? easing(pct / 100) * 100 : pct}%`;                // optional easing of the lap
  el.style.zIndex = Math.floor(1 + (pct / 100) * 10);                                   // rolling z: the lead item is on top
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; or one tick as the lead tile crosses the loop.
moves.notesHtml:
The stage is the original's responsive mode: the 996 x 330 box scales by min(vw/996, vh/330) * 1.05 and is centred. The tiles are 56 x 56 box px. The path is M1 209.434C58.5872 255.935 387.926 325.938 482.583 209.434C600.905 63.8051 525.516 -43.2211 427.332 19.9613C329.149 83.1436 352.902 242.723 515.041 267.302C644.752 286.966 943.56 181.94 995 156.5.

Option: one element along the path (the original's element-along-svg-path). One item, no repeat. Its progress is duration 4 s, linear, looping: offsetDistance = ((t / 4) % 1) * 100 + '%'. The original demo runs it once, 3 s, on cubicBezier(0.757, -0.002, 0.123, 0.993): offsetDistance = cubicBezier(0.757, -0.002, 0.123, 0.993)(clamp01(t / 3)) * 100 + '%'. direction: reverse runs 100 to 0.

The numbers that make it look expensive

  • 8 percent per second: one lap in 12.4 s. The loop of the path crosses itself, so the tiles overlap and the rolling z-index decides who is above.
  • Even gap: 100 divided by the item count, so adding items tightens the chain without changing the speed.
  • Tiles are 56 px in a 996 px wide box (5.6 percent of the box width): small enough that the curve, not the tile, is the picture.
  • The ground is #fafafa (zinc-50) and the rail is invisible (showPath is off). Show it with stroke: currentColor only for a diagram.
  • Drag and hover slow-down are not ported: at rest the original has neither.

The common mistake

Moving the tiles with transform and a hand-built tangent: offset-path does the rotation and the arc length for free. Also forgetting the viewBox scale: the path is in box px, so the items and the path must share the same scaled parent. Wrap with a modulo, never reset: a reset at 100 percent shows as a jump.

Difference from the original: the tiles are lettered colour squares in place of the demo's poster images.

moves.name: simple-marquee
moves.title: Simple marquee
moves.use: three rows of tiles slide for a whole beat, left, right, left, each row four copies that wrap by one set width at 8 percent per second
moves.useWhen: a film shows a crowd, a team or a list of names that is longer than the frame: contributors, customers, guests. Rows of name tags drift past in opposite directions.
moves.sound: none.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a film shows a crowd, a team or a list of names that is longer than the frame: contributors, customers, guests. Rows of name tags drift past in opposite directions.

Look: the flat neutral ground and a centred heading. Three lanes of white name tags with a hairline ring and a faint shadow. Each tag has a round initial in a pale tint, a name in semibold and a role in muted grey, all at 3.4 u or more. The lanes fade at the left and right edges. The names are invented people.

How it moves: the heading and the lanes fade in with a 1.2 vh rise (110 ms between lanes). Then each lane drifts at 9 u a second, the lanes in alternating directions. A marquee runs at one speed, so the drift has no ease and is a function of the seek time. The whole stage leaves on leave.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const SPEED = 9;                                          // u a second; the rows run at one speed, so no ease
window.seek = (t) => rows.forEach((row, i) => { row.style.translate = `${ROWS[i].dir * SPEED * u * t}px 0`; });
arrive(lane, 150 + r * 110, { ms: 300, from: '1.2vh' });   // the lane, not the row, so the drift keeps the row's translate
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none.
moves.notesHtml:
Common mistake: tiles that are only gradients. They read as colour blobs and say nothing. Give each tag real content (an initial, a name, a role) at a readable size, and keep every row the same height and gap so the loop is clean.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.

moves.name: circling-elements
moves.title: Circling elements
moves.use: eight upright tiles orbit one point on a 120 px radius, one linear turn in 10 s
moves.useWhen: a handful of cards, logos or photos must orbit one point and stay upright: a ring around a product, a halo of integrations, a carousel that never ends. Items sit evenly on a circle and turn as one wheel, linearly, forever.
moves.sound: none; or one soft tick per tile passing the top.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a handful of cards, logos or photos must orbit one point and stay upright: a ring around a product, a halo of integrations, a carousel that never ends. Items sit evenly on a circle and turn as one wheel, linearly, forever.

Credit: port of fancy by Daniel Petho, MIT. Source: circling-elements (repo). The keyframes and the demo are the original's.

All items are position: absolute in a zero size box at the circle centre, each centred on its own point (translate: -50% -50%). The transform is the original's: turn to the angle, go out by the radius, turn back by the same angle so the item stays upright.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const RADIUS = 120, DURATION = 10, DIRECTION = 1;          // px of a 532 px tall box (scale by vh/532), seconds per turn, -1 reverses
const ease = (p) => p;                                      // "linear", the original default; any easing runs per turn
window.seek = (t) => cards.forEach((el, i) => {
  const offset = (i * 360) / cards.length;                  // start angle: even spacing
  const a = DIRECTION * (offset + 360 * ease(((t / DURATION) % 1 + 1) % 1));
  el.style.transform = `rotate(${a}deg) translate(${RADIUS * P}px, 0) rotate(${-a}deg)`;
});
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; or one soft tick per tile passing the top.
moves.notesHtml:
Eight 112 px tiles on a 120 px radius overlap by design: the later item in the list is on top. The direction is clockwise on screen (rotate grows clockwise with y down).

The numbers that make it look expensive

  • 10 s per turn, linear: slow enough to read each tile, with no ease so the ring never seems to breathe.
  • Radius 120 against 112 px tiles: the ring is almost closed, tiles touch their neighbours at the corners.
  • 360 divided by the count: add a tile and the angles redistribute. Eight is the demo's count.
  • With an easing each turn starts and ends slow: a stepped, ratcheting feel. Keep linear for a calm ring.
  • Hover pause is not ported (no cursor in a film).

The common mistake

Rotating the wrapper: the tiles turn with it and look upside down at the bottom. Keep the counter-rotation in the same transform. Also putting transform-origin somewhere other than the item centre.

Difference from the original: the tiles are lettered colour squares in place of the demo's photos.

moves.name: css-box
moves.title: CSS box
moves.use: a 200 px cube of bold type turns to another face on a stiff overdamped spring (stiffness 100, damping 30, no overshoot) under perspective 600
moves.useWhen: a cuboid must turn to show another face: a product block with a message on each side, a block that turns to the next fact. A solid matte blue block with six real faces, sharp lit edges, big clean white type (12.5 u) on each side and a soft shadow on the table. It turns a quarter turn at a time on a stiff, overdamped spring and stops with no overshoot.
moves.sound: none; or one soft knock as each face lands (about 0.5 s after the jump).
moves.useHtml:
Use when a cuboid must turn to show another face: a product block with a message on each side, a block that turns to the next fact. A solid matte blue block with six real faces, sharp lit edges, big clean white type (12.5 u) on each side and a soft shadow on the table. It turns a quarter turn at a time on a stiff, overdamped spring and stops with no overshoot.

The spring values (stiffness 100, damping 30) come from the CSSBox component of fancy by Daniel Petho (MIT, source). The faces, the light and the look are our own.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const STIFFNESS = 100, DAMPING = 30;                    // damping ratio 1.5: no bounce
const YAW = [[0, 0], [0.7, 90], [2.0, 180], [3.3, 270]]; // [second, degrees]: one jump of the target each
const yaw = REST + track(t, YAW, STIFFNESS, DAMPING);    // REST = -28 shows the front and one side
// light from the upper left front: a face is darker as its turned normal leaves the light
shade.style.opacity = 0.5 * (1 - Math.max(0, dot(normal, light)));
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; or one soft knock as each face lands (about 0.5 s after the jump).
moves.notesHtml:
How it looks and moves

  • Six faces in one preserve-3d block, each pushed out by half the edge (56 u, 56 percent of the frame height, about 75 percent on screen with the perspective). The camera looks down 17 degrees, so the top and two sides show.
  • Faces are satin paint with a soft gradient across each face (lighter top left, darker bottom right) from one key light. The light comes from the upper left front, so the top is brightest and the right side darkest. A 0.16 u lighter line runs inside each edge. The shade is under the type, so the white stays white.
  • A faint reflection of the block lies under it: a mirrored copy of the four sides at 0.13 opacity, each face masked to fade out away from the base. It carries no type.
  • The contact shadow is a soft radial pool on the table, 1.8 times the edge wide, darkest under the block (0.55 alpha in light, 0.85 in dark).
  • The block turns about its vertical axis only. Each jump is one quarter turn (half done in 0.2 s, still by 0.7 s). The order of the faces on screen is Build, Render, Edit, Ship.
  • Only the stage fades in and out. An opacity animation on the 3D block would flatten it.

The common mistake

Using an eased CSS transition: it stops dead at each target and cannot take a second jump in flight. Use the spring on the angle. Also skip backface-visibility: hidden and the faces show through the block. Never name a custom property --edge or --surface in a demo: demo.css already owns them.

moves.name: pixelate-svg-filter
moves.title: Pixelate SVG filter
moves.use: a photo breaks into square blocks that grow and shrink with one number, size = x / 30 through a convolve, tile and dilate SVG filter
moves.useWhen: a photo or a clip must break into blocks and clear again: a censor, a retro reveal, a resolve from mosaic to sharp, a scrub of the pixel size with the cursor. The block size is one number, and the picture stays live under it.
moves.sound: none; or a rising tick that follows the block size.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a photo or a clip must break into blocks and clear again: a censor, a retro reveal, a resolve from mosaic to sharp, a scrub of the pixel size with the cursor. The block size is one number, and the picture stays live under it.

Credit: port of fancy by Daniel Petho, MIT. Source: pixelate-svg-filter (repo). The filter graph and the demo mapping are the original's.

Put filter: url(#pixelate-filter) on the wrapper of the picture. The filter averages with a 3 x 3 convolution, floods a one pixel point, tiles it at size, keeps the average under each tile point, and dilates each point by size / 2 into a block. With crossLayers two more passes tile at half width and half height and sit under the main one, so the blocks cover the edges.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const SIZE_PER_PX = 1 / 30;                                    // the demo: block size = pointer x / 30, clamped 1..64
const MOUSE_X = [[0, 60], [0.4, 60], [2.2, 600], [2.5, 600], [4.3, 60], [4.8, 60]];   // px from the left of the 500 px box
window.seek = (t) => {
  const size = Math.min(Math.max(kf(t, MOUSE_X, 'easeInOutSine') * SIZE_PER_PX, 1), 64);
  c0.setAttribute('width', size);  c0.setAttribute('height', size);          // first layer (feComposite)
  c1.setAttribute('width', size / 2); c1.setAttribute('height', size);       // crossLayers: tile half width
  c2.setAttribute('width', size);  c2.setAttribute('height', size / 2);      // crossLayers: tile half height
  for (const m of [m0, m1, m2]) m.setAttribute('radius', size / 2);          // feMorphology dilate
};
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none; or a rising tick that follows the block size.
moves.notesHtml:
The size is a pure function of the second: seek forward and back and the frame is the same. The filter units are the element's own CSS pixels, so a scaled stage (scale on the 500 x 530 stage) scales the blocks with the picture.

The numbers that make it look expensive

  • Size is pointer x divided by 30: a 500 px sweep goes from 1 to 16.7 px blocks, a sweep past the edge reaches 20.
  • Dilate radius is half the size and the composite regions are size x size: the blocks are square, not smeared.
  • crossLayers on: three tile grids merged, so no gap between blocks and no dark seams at the picture edge.
  • Ease the sweep (sine in and out): blocks that grow at a constant rate look mechanical, a swell reads as a breath.
  • Hold at a small size before the sweep and after it: the mosaic reads as a state, not a glitch.

The common mistake

Starting at size 1. Below size 1.5 the dilate radius is under 1 px and the original filter draws nothing, so the picture disappears for the first third of the pointer range. Start at 2 or more (x 60). Also animating size with a CSS transition: the attribute is not a CSS property, so set it each frame. Safari does not support this graph.

Difference from the original: the demo plays a looping video from a CDN, ours is a still photo (the filter is the same). The pointer is a time table of x values. The clip stays on a 500 x 530 stage in the middle of the frame.

moves.name: photo-particles
moves.title: Photo particles
moves.use: a real photo (filaments, veins, scales) is sampled into 120 000 lit, coloured points that gather from a seeded scatter over 1.5 s and then breathe, filmed through the lens with the film-halation look
moves.useWhen: a particle film needs the real detail of a subject (veins, scales, fibres, filaments) that a hand-modelled shape cannot give: sample a photo into 120 000 points, let them gather from a seeded scatter into the photo's form over 1.5 s, then hold them breathing for 1.5 s. Each point keeps its photo colour and a normal from the luma gradient, so a key light shapes the form.
moves.sound: a soft rising swell under the gather that ends on the settle, no hit; the breathing after it is silent.
moves.useHtml: Use when a particle film needs the real detail of a subject (veins, scales, fibres, filaments) that a hand-modelled shape cannot give: sample a photo into 120 000 points, let them gather from a seeded scatter into the photo's form over 1.5 s, then hold them breathing for 1.5 s. Each point keeps its photo colour and a normal from the luma gradient, so a key light shapes the form.
moves.codeHtml:
js
import { imagePoints, regions } from '/core/surfaces/image-points.js';
const cloud = imagePoints(img, { count: 120000, seed: 7, threshold: 0.03, gamma: 1.0, edgeBoost: 0.6, depthScale: 0.35 });
// cloud.positions x,y,z (long side -1..1, y up)   cloud.colors r,g,b 0..1   cloud.normals unit x,y,z   cloud.luma 0..1
geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(cloud.positions, 3));
geometry.setAttribute('a_color', new THREE.BufferAttribute(cloud.colors, 3));
geometry.setAttribute('a_normal', new THREE.BufferAttribute(cloud.normals, 3));
// vertex shader: gather by a per-point delay (seeded 0..1), light by the normal, breathe on the seek time
//   float u = clamp((u_progress - delay * 0.4) / 0.6, 0.0, 1.0);
//   vec3 p = mix(start, position, u);
//   float lit = 0.2 + 0.75 * max(dot(normalize(a_normal), normalize(u_key)), 0.0);
vawe.onFrame(async (t) => { u_progress.value = easeFn('land')(Math.min(1, t / 1.5)); render(); await cam.draw(t); });
const cam = lens(canvasSource(renderer.domElement), { look: 'film-halation', grain: 0 });   // film the points through the lens
moves.soundHtml: Sound: a soft rising swell under the gather that ends on the settle, no hit; the breathing after it is silent.
moves.notesHtml:
Options

  • count (300000), seed: the same inputs give the same cloud. The scatter you gather from comes from rng(seed) of core/motion/springs.js.
  • threshold (0.04): pixels darker than this get no point. gamma (1.6): how strongly bright areas pull points. A nebula wants 1.0 so the faint orange filaments keep points.
  • edgeBoost (0.5): more points on strong luma edges, so silhouettes and veins stay crisp.
  • mask: a second image. Its alpha limits the points when it has any transparent pixel, else its luma does. Use it to cut the subject from its background.
  • depth: a depth image, linear 0 (near) to 1 (far) in red. Without it depth is the luma. depthScale (0.5) sets the z span.
  • jitter (0.6 px): spreads a point off its pixel centre so the points do not line up on the pixel grid.
  • regions(labelImage, ['#ff0000', [0, 0, 255]], cloud): for each point, the index of the label colour under it. A film moves the parts apart: an eye's lid and iris, a manta's wings and body. Paint the label image flat, at the aspect of the photo.

Colours are sRGB as stored in the photo, so a shader that outputs them directly shows the photo's colour. Additive blending sums overlapping points: on a dense photo lower the point size or the light gain, or the filaments burn to white.

The clip is dense, so bin/vawe moves encodes it again at a higher CRF to fit its 2 MB budget (CRF 31, 1.3 MB; the CRF is in clips.lock.json). Grain is off in the demo for the same reason.

Measured: 1 000 000 points from a 2048 by 1536 image take about 0.5 s. The demo builds its cloud on the first seek of each page, so every render slice pays about 1 s once. Load the photo inside the frame hook, not with a top-level await: the renderer seeks the first frame before a module that waits has finished, and that frame is black.

The photo is NASA, ESA, J. Hester and A. Loll (Arizona State University), the Hubble mosaic of the Crab Nebula, public domain. The source is in demo/assets/photos/credits.json.

moves.name: media-between-text
moves.title: Media between text
moves.use: a picture grows from zero width inside a line of type on a 0.4 s critical spring and closes on a 0.3 s tween, the words part and wrap
moves.useWhen: a line of text has a gap that a picture can fill on hover or on a beat: "that's a nice ( ) chair!". The line stays one line and the picture opens inside it.
moves.sound: none.
moves.useHtml:
Use when a line of text has a gap that a picture can fill on hover or on a beat: "that's a nice ( ) chair!". The line stays one line and the picture opens inside it.

Look: one line of light grotesque type, large, on warm bone paper. A rounded photo, 28 u tall (2.8 times the type size of 10 u, so taller than the cap height), sits between two parentheses. A small dark pointer shows the cause: the picture opens while the pointer is over the line and closes when it leaves.

How it moves: on enter the photo width goes from 0 to 34 u on a critically damped spring (stiffness 532.6, damping 46.15, no bounce, about 0.4 s). On leave it closes in 0.3 s on EASE.land. The text on both sides re-centres with it, so the line never wraps. The pointer travels between stops on EASE.land. The clip hovers twice.
moves.codeHtml:
js
const OPEN = { k: 532.6, d: 46.15 }, CLOSE_S = 0.3, HOVERS = [[0.55, 1.95], [2.8, 3.75]];   // [enter, leave] in seconds
const widthAt = (t) => {
  for (let i = HOVERS.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const [enter, out] = HOVERS[i];
    if (t >= out) return WIDTH * (1 - easeFn('land')(Math.min((t - out) / CLOSE_S, 1)));
    if (t >= enter) return WIDTH * spring(t - enter, OPEN.k, OPEN.d);   // spring from core/motion/springs.js
  }
  return 0;
};
window.seek = (t) => { media.style.width = `${widthAt(t)}px`; };       // media: overflow hidden, the img inside keeps its own width
moves.soundHtml: Sound: none.
moves.notesHtml:
Common mistake: a photo smaller than the text. It reads as a speck, and the line wraps while the gap opens. Make the photo taller than the cap height, keep the line on one row, and open the width, not the height.

Looks (ground, type, radius, accent) live in demo/demo.css; this snippet keeps neutral tokens.
